title: Feat project configuration
description: One project's configuration, as authored in ~/.config/feat/projects/<project-id>.yaml. The file name must match project.id. This schema is a draft for editor support; feat doctor performs the semantic validation, and some of its rules cannot be expressed here.

version.description: Configuration schema version. This build understands 1 only.

repositories.description: Git repositories participating in the project, keyed by project-local identifier.

checks.description: Verification commands per repository, keyed by repository identifier.

safeIdentifier.description: An identifier that is safe in paths, branch names, tmux metadata, and Compose project names.

duration.description: A Go duration such as "5s", "250ms", or "1m30s".

path.description: A host path. A leading "~" expands to the home directory of the user running the daemon.

containerPath.description: An absolute path inside the agent's execution environment.

id.description: Identifies the project locally. It must match the file name.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to the identifier.

primary_repository.description: The editable repository a task works in by default. It must be one a task can edit.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to the repository identifier.

host_path.description: The ordinary checkout on this machine.

default_branch.description: The branch a base policy resolves against. Defaults to "main".

remote.description: The Git remote fetched before a base is resolved. Defaults to "origin".

default_access.description: How the repository takes part in a task by default. Required rather than defaulted: whether an agent may write to a repository is not a decision to make on the user's behalf.

repositoryAgent.description: Where the agent's own execution environment puts this repository. It is separate from the runtime object below because the two are different questions with different owners: where the agent's devcontainer mounts a worktree is your free choice, and where an application's own services expect their source is a fact about its Compose files.

container_path.description: Where task worktrees are mounted in the devcontainer. Required for every repository a task can select when agent.execution.mode is "devcontainer", rejected under "host", and agent container paths must not overlap.

repositoryForge.description: Where this repository's merge requests are opened. Omit it for a repository Feat never publishes. It is per repository because a repository lives on exactly one forge and a task may span several, and it is separate from the project's tracker because a forge hosts code and a tracker holds tickets: the two coincide only where a forge hosts its own issues.

kind.description: The forge this repository publishes to. It is declared rather than guessed: a self-hosted instance is not recognisable from its remote, and guessing wrong would open a merge request somewhere you did not mean.

repositoryRuntime.description: What this repository contributes to the project's application runtime. Omit it for a repository whose code no service runs. A runtime is composed of its repositories: each brings its own Compose files, and Feat generates the include document that joins them, so nothing relative ever crosses a repository boundary.

compose_files.description: The Compose files this repository brings. A relative path resolves against the repository's own checkout, which is also the project directory Feat gives its include entry.

container_path.description: Where this repository's own services expect their source. Feat mounts each task worktree there, replacing whatever the repository's Compose files mounted at that path. It requires services to mount it in.

services.description: The services that run this repository's code, which Feat manages for a task. Two repositories may name one service: a service running an application and a shared library runs the code of both, at their own container paths.

reachable.description: The services of this repository you reach from this machine. Each must be one of the services above.

base_policy.description: How a task's base commit is resolved. Feat records the resulting commit, not the ref.

fetch_before_task.description: Fetch configured remotes before resolving bases. Fetching never changes the ordinary checkout.

branch_template.description: Generates task branch names. It must contain {task_id} or {task_key}, or two tasks would share a branch. Placeholders: {project_id}, {task_id}, {task_key}, {repository_id}, {slug}.

worktree_root.description: Generates the directory holding a task's worktrees. It must contain {task_id} or {task_key}, must not be rooted at a shared directory, and must not overlap a repository checkout: Feat removes worktrees under this root during cleanup. Placeholders: {project_id}, {task_id}, {task_key}, {repository_id}.

provider.description: The agent adapter. Claude Code is the only provider in v0.

mode.description: Where the agent runs. "host" has no container boundary; "devcontainer" runs the agent in a configured Compose service. The remaining fields in this object apply to "devcontainer" only and are rejected under "host".

compose_files.description: The Compose files defining the devcontainer.

service.description: The Compose service the agent runs in.

user.description: The container user the agent runs as. It must not be root.

working_directory.description: The agent's working directory inside the devcontainer. It must be inside a repository's container_path. Defaults to the primary repository's container_path.

control_path.description: Where the task control workspace is mounted. It must not overlap a repository mount.

config_volume.description: A dedicated Docker volume for Claude's configuration, which keeps one interactive login out of the user's own ~/.claude. Optional: without it Feat mounts nothing and leaves the provider's configuration to the project's own Compose files.

config_path.description: Where config_volume is mounted in the devcontainer, and the value of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. It must not overlap a repository mount or the control path.

idle_grace_period.description: How long an end-of-turn signal waits before the task is reported idle. Idle never means complete.

capabilities.description: What the agent's environment may reach. The capabilities are independent: full Git access says nothing about Docker. Each accepts one value, because Feat has no mechanism that varies them, and recording another value would be a promise the binary does not keep.

docker.description: The agent never receives a Docker socket or a Docker CLI that reaches the host; only the trusted host runs Docker Compose.

network.description: Feat does not implement network restriction and does not claim data-loss prevention.

git.description: A native Git worktree shares repository metadata with the agent, which Feat does not restrict.

runtime.description: The application services a task may run. Omit this object for a project with no application runtime. What the application is made of is on the repositories that bring it: see repositories.<id>.runtime.

provider.description: The runtime adapter. Docker Compose is the only provider in v0.

start_policy.description: When services start. In v0 they start by explicit user action only.

static_overrides.description: User-authored override files, applied after Feat's generated include of the repositories' own Compose files and before its generated task override. A relative path inside one resolves against Feat's own generated directory, so write them absolute.

env_files.description: Host-side environment files passed to Docker Compose by path. Feat records the paths and never reads their contents.

project_name_template.description: Generates the Compose project name, which is what makes a runtime action affect one task and no other. It must contain {task_id} or {task_key}, and must expand to a name Compose accepts. Placeholders: {project_id}, {task_id}, {task_key}.

port_range.description: The host ports Feat publishes this project's reachable services on, written "<first>-<last>". One port is allocated per reachable service per task and released when that task's runtime is destroyed, which is what lets several tasks run the whole application at once.

bind_address.description: The host address an allocated port is published on when the project's own Compose files named none. It must be a literal IP address. The default binds this machine alone; "0.0.0.0" binds every interface the machine has, which makes the service reachable from the whole network it is on and from every container on it, including other tasks' agents. An address a project's own file named is kept as it is.

tracker.description: Where this project's tickets come from. Omit it for a project whose tasks are all written by hand. It is per project because the thing a ticket seeds is a task: trackers do not agree on where a ticket lives — issues hang off a repository, stories off a workspace, a board off an organisation — so this says how to obtain a list, and the scope of that list belongs to the command.

kind.description: How tickets are obtained. A configured command is the only kind: a tracker CLI already prints JSON, so a native adapter would add nothing but a mapping from its field names to the shape Feat publishes.

command.description: A command printing your tickets as JSON conforming to schema/feat-tickets.schema.json. Feat passes it no filter and no placeholder: which tickets are yours is the command's decision, and feat doctor checks that what it prints is the published shape.

id.description: Identifies the check within its repository.
